script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 27. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Why do Japanese bow and Americans shake hands?  Why do some cultures eat with hands and others with utensils?  Culture is the invisible fabric of shared assumptions, practices, and values that make groups distinct—and that shape you more than you realize.

You don't notice your culture until you encounter a different one. The fish doesn't see the water. Travel, immigration, or exposure to difference reveals assumptions you didn't know you had. Culture affects more than customs—it shapes perception itself.  Studies show people from different cultures literally see images differently, prioritize different information, and process emotions in distinct ways.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You swim in culture like fish swim in water.  It shapes you even when you don't notice.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Cultural Assumption - What's Invisible?.

Here's your activity: Identify one thing you consider 'normal' that other cultures do differently—meal times, personal space, communication style. Question it: why do you do it this way? Is it better, or just familiar? This practice reveals invisible cultural programming. This helps you identify hidden cultural assumptions.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what makes groups different can be applied to cultural assumption - what's invisible?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
